2027-05-04.title: Tuesday of the fifth week after Qyomtho
readings: Gentle like a nurse; sharing not only the gospel but our own selves
“Whoever keeps my word will never see death”
2027-05-04.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Fifth Sunday after Qyomtho; Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord, is on Thursday 6 May.
2027-05-04.verse: So deeply do we care for you that we are determined to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves, because you have become very dear to us.
theo: Thessalonica was one of Paul's shortest missions. He had arrived there bruised from Philippi, preached for a few weeks, and was forced to leave by night. Now, writing back to the young church, he remembers how he had lived among them, and the letter becomes a portrait of a pastor's heart. “You yourselves know, brothers and sisters, that our coming to you was not in vain, but though we had already suffered and been shamefully mistreated at Philippi, as you know, we had courage in our God to declare to you the gospel of God in spite of great opposition.” The courage did not come from Paul's temperament; it came “in our God.” And his motive was clean: “we speak, not to please mortals, but to please God who tests our hearts.” He had not used flattery, had not looked for money, had not sought praise. Every preacher, every catechism teacher, every parent who speaks of God at home can examine himself by these lines. Am I trying to be liked, or trying to be faithful? God tests the heart, and the heart is where the Gospel either rings true or sounds hollow.

Then Paul uses two images that are surprising from a man so often pictured as stern. “But we were gentle among you, like a nurse tenderly caring for her own children.” And a few lines later: “we dealt with each one of you like a father with his children, urging and encouraging you and pleading that you lead a life worthy of God.” Mother and father together: tenderness and firmness, care and challenge. At the centre is the verse that sums up all ministry: “So deeply do we care for you that we are determined to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves, because you have become very dear to us.” A message alone is not enough. The Gospel travels from person to person through shared lives, through time given, meals eaten together, nights of work so as not to be a burden. Paul again mentions his manual labour: “we worked night and day, so that we might not burden any of you while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.” St Gregory the Great wrote that the pastor must be near to each one in compassion and raised above all in contemplation, so that he can carry the weaknesses of others in his own heart (Pastoral Rule II.5, in substance).

In the Gospel the argument in the temple grows sharp. Some of Jesus' hearers say, “Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?” When John speaks of “the Jews” in passages like this he means those among the leaders and hearers who opposed Jesus in that hour, not the Jewish people as a whole, of whom Jesus himself, his Mother and all the apostles were members; the Church firmly rejects any blame of the Jewish people for these quarrels (Nostra Aetate 4; CCC 597). Jesus does not answer insult with insult. He says simply, “I do not have a demon; but I honor my Father,” and then he makes one of the great promises of the fourth Gospel: “Very truly, I tell you, whoever keeps my word will never see death.” In the season of Qyomtho we hear it with Easter ears. The one who says it has already passed through death and come out the other side. To keep his word is to be joined to his risen life, so that bodily death, when it comes, is no longer the end but a door. Keeping his word begins in small things: the word of forgiveness I must speak, the word of truth I must not bend. Like Paul at Thessalonica, we keep it best when we share it with our whole life.
outline: Ask: when I speak of God, am I trying to please people or God?
Point 1 · To please God who tests our hearts
Courage in God, and a clean motive.
Point 2 · Gentle like a nurse, firm like a father
Sharing the Gospel and our own selves.
The risen Lord's promise against death.
“Not only the gospel of God but also our own selves.”
live: Give someone in your family or parish an unhurried hour this week: a visit, a meal, a long listening.
Choose one saying of Jesus from this week's readings and live it deliberately for a whole day.
2027-05-04.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you promised that whoever keeps your word will never see death. Give us courage in God to speak your Gospel, and purity of heart to seek only to please the Father who tests our hearts. Make our priests, teachers and parents gentle as a nurse and firm as a father, ready to share not only your word but their own selves. Keep us in your word, that we may share your risen life for ever. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar Christ does what Paul could only imitate: he shares with us not only his word but his own self, his Body and Blood, in the Holy Qurbono.

quick: Paul preached at Thessalonica with courage in God, seeking to please not mortals but God who tests our hearts.
He was gentle like a nurse and firm like a father, sharing not only the Gospel but his own self.
Jesus answers insult with truth: whoever keeps my word will never see death.
2027-05-04.action: Give someone an unhurried hour of your time this week.
2027-05-04.question: Do I share only words about God, or also my time and my life?

family.explain: St Paul says he was gentle with the people of Thessalonica, like a nurse taking care of little children. He loved them so much that he gave them not only the good news of Jesus but his own time and his whole heart. In a family we do this for one another every day: mothers, fathers, grandparents and children all care for each other.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, teachers and parents, that they may be gentle and strong like St Paul.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family needs more of our time this week?”

illus: A young priest was sent to a small parish in the hills of Idukki where many families had moved away. In his first months he preached careful sermons and few people came. An old sacristan advised him: “Father, before they listen to you, they need to see you.” So he began walking every afternoon to two or three houses, sitting on the veranda, drinking the black tea he was given and listening to stories of rubber prices and children abroad. By the next Easter the church was fuller. One woman told him, “We came because you came first.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, your word is life. Teach us to keep it and to share it with our whole lives. Amen.
share: We speak, not to please mortals, but to please God who tests our hearts (1 Thessalonians 2:4). Whom am I trying to please?
Gentle among you, like a nurse tenderly caring for her own children (1 Thessalonians 2:7). Who has cared for my faith with such tenderness?
Whoever keeps my word will never see death (John 8:51). Which word of Jesus am I trying to keep this week?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your word.
interc: For bishops, priests and catechists, that they may share the Gospel and their own selves with their people.
For parents and grandparents, who pass on the faith with gentleness and firmness.
For those who are insulted or misunderstood for doing good, that they may answer like Jesus, with truth and without bitterness.
For friendship and respect between Christians and the Jewish people.
For the dying, that they may hold to the word of Christ and pass through death into life.
pm.close: Father, your Son honoured you in all things and promised life to those who keep his word. Give us pure hearts that seek only your pleasure, and generous hearts that share themselves with others, until we see you face to face. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! St Paul remembers his short time in Thessalonica. He had been mistreated at Philippi, yet he says: we had courage in our God to declare to you the gospel of God (1 Thessalonians 2:2). And his motive was pure: not to please mortals, but to please God who tests our hearts (2:4).

Then he uses two tender pictures. We were gentle among you, like a nurse tenderly caring for her own children. And: we dealt with each one of you like a father with his children (2:7, 11). He adds: we were determined to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves (2:8). The Gospel is passed on not only by words but by lives given.

In the Gospel some of Jesus' hearers insult him: you are a Samaritan and have a demon. Jesus does not insult them back. He says: I honor my Father. And he gives a great promise: whoever keeps my word will never see death (John 8:51). The one who says this has already risen from the dead.

So let us keep his word, and let us share it as Paul did, with our time and our love. Parents, teachers, priests: be gentle and firm, and give yourselves. And let us all remember: in Christ, death is not the end. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Who takes care of you when you are sick? Maybe your mother or your grandmother sits beside you and gives you medicine and soup. St Paul says he loved the people of Thessalonica like that, as gently as a nurse with little children. He gave them his time and his whole heart. Jesus says that if we keep his word, we will live for ever with him. Let us keep Jesus' words and share his love gently with everyone.

intro: Theme: “Not only the gospel of God but also our own selves.”
On Tuesday of the fifth week after Qyomtho: the pure motive of the preacher, the gentleness of a nurse and the firmness of a father, and the word that conquers death.

points.h: To please God who tests our hearts
q: for the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
Am I now seeking human approval, or God’s approval? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
points.apply: Before you speak about God or give advice this week, ask silently: am I seeking to please God or to be admired?

points.h: Gentle like a nurse, firm like a father
q: He will feed his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them in his bosom, and gently lead the mother sheep.
No one has greater love than this, to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.
points.apply: Give one person an hour of undivided attention this week, without looking at your phone.

points.h: Whoever keeps my word will never see death
sub: The promise of the Risen One.
Keeping his word in small things.
q: I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live,
I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live,
points.apply: Choose one word of Jesus and practise it deliberately for one whole day.

concl: The Gospel passes from life to life when its messengers give themselves.
Christ, risen from death, gives life to all who keep his word.
2027-05-04.resolve: Seek to please God, share yourself generously, answer insults with truth, and keep one word of Jesus each day.
